notes.4: For this exercise, candidates were required to read a more extended text about Sophie who wrote about her experience of working in a hairdressing salon. The text used largely familiar vocabulary. The text was written in the first person, and the questions used the third person. Most questions could be answered by lifting a small number of words from the text, but some answers also required a minor manipulation. If candidates choose to lift more than is required to answer questions, they must make any manipulation needed in the extra material, for example replacing je with elle and changing the verb if necessary. Candidates are therefore advised to answer with the minimum number of words. Overall, 4(c), 4(f), 4(g) and 4(j) were answered well. For 4(a), the question word quand was not always understood. Some candidates also omitted il y a in their answer and could not gain the mark. Some candidates did not understand qui in 4(b). For 4(d), some candidates answered with washing or cleaning, but these were not tâches habituelles that the question referred to. Weaker candidates could not manipulate the text correctly to answer 4(e). Some candidates added information to 4(h) which invalidated their answer because they did not manipulate the extra information. All that was required was nettoyer le salon. For 4(i), some candidates answered with the wrong part of the text and thought Sophie was tired because there was hair everywhere. For 4(k), some candidates could not manipulate mon to son or misplaced the word propre which changed the meaning of their answer (ouvrir un salon propre). �PAGE�15
notes.5: In this question, candidates had to match a series of descriptions with statements from people looking for a camping site. Candidates had five people and eight descriptions to choose from. Candidates had to process a variety of information and match several requirements whilst eliminating responses that did not fit. The question is aimed at the higher grades, and candidates with a wide range of vocabulary and knowledge of synonyms performed well on this section. Each person’s statement gave specific requirements for the sort of camping site they were looking for, such as time of year, location and activities available. It is important for candidates to note that these details excluded all answers except the correct one. Candidates need to ensure they consider all the information given as this is not a gist comprehension question and a global understanding of the texts will not be sufficient. Some candidates could not answer 5(b) and 5(e) correctly, but there was no pattern of incorrect answers.
notes.6: This final exercise about Mario who experienced his first marathon was intended to be the most challenging part of the paper. About half the questions could be answered with a careful lift from the text and the others needed a small manipulation of the text. Few candidates achieved full marks. Minor spelling errors were usually ignored unless they formed a different word in French. Verbs do not necessarily have to be correct to score a mark, but the tense chosen must usually be appropriate to the question. For 6(a), some candidates added extra information which invalidated their answer. Stronger candidates answered 6(b) correctly and only the strongest candidates successfully manipulated the text to answer 6(c). For 6(d), candidates often omitted the subject or the auxiliary verb. Overall, 6(e) was answered well. Many candidates could not answer 6(f) correctly as their answer was not precise enough. For 6(g), some candidates wrote ça famille and invalidated their answer. Many candidates did not answer 6(h) correctly. Only the strongest candidates answered 6(i) successfully. Many added invalidating material, such as reference to fatigue or les jambes tremblantes. �PAGE�16
notes.key_messages:
To maximise their chances of success on this paper, candidates should:
• answer all questions
• answer questions in French as briefly as possible
• check all their answers for accuracy, legibility and completeness.
